_comment: The golden correctness harness. Every question carries hand-reviewed reference SQL over the jaffle-golden seed (dev.* marts of the real jaffle-shop-duckdb project, 12 customers). At test time the reference SQL is executed against the same seeded engine the server queries, and the run's result rows must equal it. `columns` maps each reference column to the names the product may legitimately use for it. `ordered` means row order is part of the answer. `tier` is the trust the answer must carry. `outcome` is 'rows' unless a clarification or an honest gap is the correct answer. Identity rule: rankings of customers/products are keyed by their id and display the name; a result may carry the id, the name, or both, and matches the reference through either.

questions.question: who are the top customers for beverage product category
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.is_drink_item THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY drink_revenue DESC LIMIT 10
questions.note: Both are correct: the certified top_beverage_customers block served as published (it groups by customer name; the caveat that two customers sharing a name would merge is recorded on the answer), or a governed semantic/relational answer keyed by customer id with the name displayed. The identity rule binds what the pipeline composes, not what the team certified.

questions.question: who are the top customers
questions.sql: SELECT customer_id, customer_name, lifetime_spend FROM dev.customers ORDER BY lifetime_spend DESC LIMIT 10
questions.note: Lifetime spend including tax is the customers mart definition; pretax spend is an acceptable reading and is listed as an alias because the ranking is identical on this seed. "Top customers" names no measure; the certified customer_profile ordering (lifetime spend) or the lifetime_spend metric are governed readings, and one bounded clarification between gross and pretax spend is also correct.

questions.question: top 5 customers by revenue
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

alternatives.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, SUM(o.order_total) AS order_total FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY order_total DESC LIMIT 5

questions.note: The governed Revenue term admits gross order revenue (order_total) as well as pretax product revenue; both readings are accepted.

questions.question: beverage revenue
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN is_drink_item THEN product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items

questions.question: total revenue
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items
questions.note: The governed Revenue term defines BOTH gross order revenue (orders.order_total, incl. tax) and product revenue (order_items.product_price, pretax). Either governed reading, or one bounded clarification between them, is correct; a silent third definition is not.

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(order_total) AS revenue FROM dev.orders

questions.question: revenue by month
questions.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', ordered_at) AS month, SUM(product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
questions.note: The certified monthly_revenue block sums order_total (incl. tax); the semantic revenue metric sums product_price. Either is a governed monthly revenue answer; the harness accepts the one whose label matches and checks its numbers against that definition.

alternatives.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', ordered_at) AS month, SUM(order_total) AS gross_revenue FROM dev.orders GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

questions.question: how many orders did each customer place
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name

questions.question: what is the total revenue by location
questions.sql: SELECT l.location_id, l.location_name, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id GROUP BY l.location_id, l.location_name

alternatives.sql: SELECT l.location_id, l.location_name, SUM(o.order_total) AS order_total FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.locations l ON o.location_id = l.location_id GROUP BY l.location_id, l.location_name

questions.note: The governed Revenue term admits gross order revenue (order_total) as well as pretax product revenue; both readings are accepted.

questions.question: top 10 products by revenue
questions.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10

questions.question: beverage revenue by product
questions.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.product_price) AS beverage_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.is_drink_item GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY beverage_revenue DESC

alternatives.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.is_drink_item THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS beverage_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name

questions.note: Either the certified block (drink products only) or a governed answer scoping the revenue measure to drink items across every product is a correct reading.

questions.question: revenue by product type
questions.sql: SELECT p.product_type, SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_type

questions.question: compare food and drink revenue
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN is_food_item THEN product_price ELSE 0 END) AS food_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN is_drink_item THEN product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items

questions.question: what is the total revenue for "Ryan Byrd"
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.customer_name = 'Ryan Byrd'
questions.note: A quoted literal is a filter on the customer name. 'Revenue' follows the governed term: order revenue (incl. tax) or product revenue (pretax) are both governed readings; clarifying between them is also correct.

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(o.order_total) AS revenue FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.customer_name = 'Ryan Byrd'
SELECT SUM(lifetime_spend) AS lifetime_spend FROM dev.customers WHERE customer_name = 'Ryan Byrd'

questions.question: what is the "Ryan byrd" revenue by total revenue and beverage revenue? give me both
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(oi.product_price) AS revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.is_drink_item THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE lower(c.customer_name) = 'ryan byrd'
questions.note: Two measures of the same customer, one filter matched case-insensitively. 'Total revenue' may follow either governed reading of the Revenue term (order total incl. tax, or pretax product revenue); the beverage restriction applies only to the beverage measure.

alternatives.sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(o.order_total) FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE lower(c.customer_name)='ryan byrd') AS revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN oi.is_drink_item THEN oi.product_price ELSE 0 END) AS drink_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE lower(c.customer_name) = 'ryan byrd'

questions.question: how many orders by customer type
questions.sql: SELECT c.customer_type, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM dev.orders o JOIN dev.customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_type

questions.question: what is the average order value
questions.sql: SELECT AVG(order_total) AS average_order_value FROM dev.orders

alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(lifetime_spend_pretax) / SUM(count_lifetime_orders) AS average_order_value FROM dev.customers

questions.note: Two governed readings: the semantic metric average_order_value is defined in dbt as lifetime_spend_pretax / count_lifetime_orders (customers grain); a plain average of order_total is the physical reading. Both are accepted; a silent third definition is not.

questions.question: how many large orders were there
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS large_orders FROM dev.orders WHERE order_total >= 20
questions.note: large_orders is a filtered metric in the semantic layer (order_total >= 20).

questions.question: drink orders by month
questions.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', ordered_at) AS month, COUNT(*) AS drink_orders FROM dev.orders WHERE is_drink_order GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

questions.question: show me the customer profile for Ryan Byrd
questions.sql: SELECT customer_name, customer_type, count_lifetime_orders, lifetime_spend FROM dev.customers WHERE customer_name = 'Ryan Byrd'
questions.note: The certified customer_profile block declares customer_name as an allowed filter; a filtered certified answer or a governed semantic answer are both correct.

questions.question: supply cost by product
questions.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(s.supply_cost) AS supply_cost FROM dev.supplies s JOIN dev.products p ON s.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name

questions.question: I need to get the bevereage catogery
questions.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.product_price) AS beverage_revenue FROM dev.order_items oi JOIN dev.products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.is_drink_item GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY beverage_revenue DESC
questions.note: Standing alone this is materially ambiguous (which measure? which grain?). A bounded clarification is correct; so is a beverage-scoped governed answer. A drink revenue table grouped by true/false is neither.

questions.question: churn rate by region
questions.note: Nothing in the project models churn or region. The correct answer is a precise gap naming the nearest vocabulary, never a fabricated query.
